tone_statements.citation: Somé, Joachim. 1998. L'orthographe pratique de l'alladian. Deuxième partie: une méthode de notation sélective des tons. Abidjan, février 1998. 34 pp. Unpublished typescript (Alliance Biblique Universelle translation consultant), PDF (2009) hosted by the Orthography Clearinghouse (CATA).
tone_statements.quote: 0.2. L’alladian est une langue à tons. Chaque mot comporte dans sa prononciation un contour mélodique appelé schème tonal, c’est-à-dire une configuration linéaire comportant: un, deux ou plusieurs tons. [...] 0.4. En résumé, on peut admettre un système intégré de quatre tonèmes en alladian. On dispose de quatre accents pour les écrire : - Accent aigu pour le ton ponctuel haut, - Accent grave pour le ton ponctuel bas, - Accent circonflexe pour le ton modulé haut-bas - Et accent horizontal à la fois pour le ton ponctuel moyen et le ton modulé moyen-bas.
tone_statements.translation: 0.2. Alladian is a tone language. Every word carries in its pronunciation a melodic contour called a tonal scheme, i.e. a linear configuration of one, two or several tones. [...] 0.4. In summary, one may posit an integrated system of four tonemes in Alladian. Four accents are available to write them: acute accent for the level high tone, grave accent for the level low tone, circumflex for the falling high-low contour tone, and a horizontal accent (macron) for both the level mid tone and the falling mid-low contour.
tone_statements.locator: §0.2 (p.5) and §0.4 (p.7); also §0.3 pp.5-6, §2.1.4 p.20 and §2.2.5 p.30 (grammatical tones)
tone_statements.summary: Four tonemes on the syllable -- level H, M, L plus falling HL (falling ML = contextual variant of M) -- with lexical minimal pairs and grammatical (floating) tones in verb conjugation (imperative II, future II, accompli), none in the noun phrase; L the most frequent tone.

sources.note: States that Alladian is a tone language with four tonemes: three level tones (high, mid, low) and a falling high-low contour; a falling mid-low contour exists but is the rarest tone, occurs only on the final syllable of polysyllables, never contrasts with mid and simplifies to mid before a following word, so it is analysed as a contextual variant of mid (§0.3); low is the most frequent tone in all positions (§0.5); minimal pairs distinguished by tone alone (§0.2, ex. [1]); ch. II: no grammatical (floating) tones in the noun constituent -- nominal prefixes and determiners carry their own base…
